deviations.title: SSH Password Authentication Disabled
deviations.reason: Not yet independently verified in this environment - gap status: non_compliant; 2 check(s) evaluated by 15-validation.sh.
deviations.risk_accepted: Not accepted - critical control, remediation via 4-ssh_hardening.sh must be completed before production sign-off.
deviations.compensating_control: 3 of 5 hospital breaches in the Crimson Tide advisory used SSH with password auth for lateral movement. Key-only auth removes the credential-stuffing/brute-force path entirely.
deviations.owner: MedDefense Infrastructure Hardening Team (James Chen, workstream owner)

deviations.title: Kernel Network Stack Hardened Against Pivoting
deviations.reason: Not yet independently verified in this environment - gap status: partially_compliant; 3 check(s) evaluated by 15-validation.sh.
deviations.risk_accepted: Not accepted - critical control, remediation via 5-sysctl_hardening.sh must be completed before production sign-off.
deviations.compensating_control: A compromised host with IP forwarding enabled becomes a router for the attacker; ICMP redirects allow traffic rerouting. Both are default-off requirements for any production Linux server.
deviations.owner: MedDefense Infrastructure Hardening Team (James Chen, workstream owner)

deviations.title: SUID/SGID Binary Whitelist Enforced
deviations.reason: Not yet independently verified in this environment - gap status: non_compliant; 1 check(s) evaluated by 15-validation.sh.
deviations.risk_accepted: Not accepted - critical control, remediation via 6-filesystem_hardening.sh must be completed before production sign-off.
deviations.compensating_control: SUID/SGID binaries outside the known-safe Ubuntu 22.04 set are the most common local privilege-escalation vector once an attacker has any shell.
deviations.owner: MedDefense Infrastructure Hardening Team (James Chen, workstream owner)

deviations.title: PAM Password Quality Policy Enforced
deviations.reason: Not yet independently verified in this environment - gap status: partially_compliant; 1 check(s) evaluated by 15-validation.sh.
deviations.risk_accepted: Not accepted - critical control, remediation via 8-pam_hardening.sh must be completed before production sign-off.
deviations.compensating_control: MedDefense currently enforces no password complexity on Linux hosts. A 14-character complexity policy directly raises the cost of the credential-based attacks documented in 3 of 5 Crimson Tide breaches.
deviations.owner: MedDefense Infrastructure Hardening Team (James Chen, workstream owner)

deviations.title: World-Writable Files Remediated and Hardened Mount Options
deviations.reason: Not yet independently verified in this environment - gap status: non_compliant; 1 check(s) evaluated by 15-validation.sh.
deviations.risk_accepted: Temporarily accepted pending remediation via 6-filesystem_hardening.sh; tracked in remediation_queue.json.
deviations.compensating_control: World-writable files let a low-privilege attacker tamper with content a privileged process later executes; noexec/nosuid/nodev on temp filesystems removes /tmp as a binary-drop staging area.
deviations.owner: MedDefense Infrastructure Hardening Team (James Chen, workstream owner)

deviations.title: Unnecessary Services Disabled (Attack Surface Reduction)
deviations.reason: Not yet independently verified in this environment - gap status: non_compliant; 1 check(s) evaluated by 15-validation.sh.
deviations.risk_accepted: Temporarily accepted pending remediation via 7-service_minimization.sh; tracked in remediation_queue.json.
deviations.compensating_control: Baseline found 24 enabled services on billing-srv-01. A billing server does not need avahi-daemon, cups or rpcbind - each is an unused, unmonitored entry point.
deviations.owner: MedDefense Infrastructure Hardening Team (James Chen, workstream owner)

deviations.title: Account Lockout on Repeated Failed Authentication
deviations.reason: Not yet independently verified in this environment - gap status: non_compliant; 1 check(s) evaluated by 15-validation.sh.
deviations.risk_accepted: Temporarily accepted pending remediation via 8-pam_hardening.sh; tracked in remediation_queue.json.
deviations.compensating_control: Without pam_faillock, an attacker with a credential list has unlimited authentication attempts. 5 attempts / 900s lockout directly closes the brute-force window Finding 009 identified.
deviations.owner: MedDefense Infrastructure Hardening Team (James Chen, workstream owner)

deviations.title: Audit Trail for Identity Files and Configuration Integrity
deviations.reason: Not yet independently verified in this environment - gap status: non_compliant; 2 check(s) evaluated by 15-validation.sh.
deviations.risk_accepted: Temporarily accepted pending remediation via 10-auditd_config.sh; tracked in remediation_queue.json.
deviations.compensating_control: Kernel-level watch rules on identity and auth configuration files are the minimum telemetry needed to detect the credential-harvesting phase of a Crimson Tide-style intrusion in real time instead of 5 days later.
deviations.owner: MedDefense Infrastructure Hardening Team (James Chen, workstream owner)

deviations.title: Host Firewall Default-Deny Inbound Policy
deviations.reason: Not yet independently verified in this environment - gap status: partially_compliant; 2 check(s) evaluated by 15-validation.sh.
deviations.risk_accepted: Temporarily accepted pending remediation via 13-firewall_baseline.sh; tracked in remediation_queue.json.
deviations.compensating_control: Service minimization (MD-CIS-008) reduces what listens; the firewall independently enforces what is reachable from the network, so a re-enabled service by mistake is still blocked at the network layer.
deviations.owner: MedDefense Infrastructure Hardening Team (James Chen, workstream owner)

deviations.title: Audit Trail for Privilege Escalation and Suspicious Tooling
deviations.reason: Not yet independently verified in this environment - gap status: non_compliant; 1 check(s) evaluated by 15-validation.sh.
deviations.risk_accepted: Accepted as lower-severity residual risk pending scheduled remediation via 10-auditd_config.sh.
deviations.compensating_control: Rated medium rather than critical because this is detective, not preventive, control - it does not stop the action, it guarantees it is not silent. Preventive controls (MD-CIS-001/002/005) carry the higher severity.
deviations.owner: MedDefense Infrastructure Hardening Team (James Chen, workstream owner)

deviations.title: Audit Telemetry Coverage Validated
deviations.reason: Not yet independently verified in this environment - gap status: not_assessed; 1 check(s) evaluated by 15-validation.sh.
deviations.risk_accepted: Accepted as lower-severity residual risk pending scheduled remediation via 11-audit_coverage_test.sh.
deviations.compensating_control: Medium severity: this control validates MD-CIS-011/013 rather than independently blocking or detecting a threat. Without it, a silently-broken auditd rule set would go unnoticed until an actual incident.
deviations.owner: MedDefense Infrastructure Hardening Team (James Chen, workstream owner)

deviations.title: Structured Log Routing and Retention
deviations.reason: Not yet independently verified in this environment - gap status: partially_compliant; 1 check(s) evaluated by 15-validation.sh.
deviations.risk_accepted: Accepted as lower-severity residual risk pending scheduled remediation via 12-log_config.sh.
deviations.compensating_control: Medium severity because default rsyslog routing already captures most events on a stock Ubuntu install; the gap is retention/rotation discipline, not total log loss - a compensating control already partially exists.
deviations.owner: MedDefense Infrastructure Hardening Team (James Chen, workstream owner)

findings.message: This release is more than 4 months old. Check the website or GitHub to see if there is an update available.
Install libpam-tmpdir to set $TMP and $TMPDIR for PAM sessions
Install apt-listbugs to display a list of critical bugs prior to each APT installation.
Install apt-listchanges to display any significant changes prior to any upgrade via APT.
Install needrestart, alternatively to debian-goodies, so that you can run needrestart after upgrades to determine which daemons are using old versions of libraries and need restarting.
Install fail2ban to automatically ban hosts that commit multiple authentication errors.
Set a password on GRUB boot loader to prevent altering boot configuration (e.g. boot in single user mode without password)
Consider hardening system services
If not required, consider explicit disabling of core dump in /etc/security/limits.conf file
Run pwck manually and correct any errors in the password file
Configure password hashing rounds in /etc/login.defs
Configure minimum password age in /etc/login.defs
Configure maximum password age in /etc/login.defs
Default umask in /etc/login.defs could be more strict like 027
To decrease the impact of a full /home file system, place /home on a separate partition
To decrease the impact of a full /tmp file system, place /tmp on a separate partition
To decrease the impact of a full /var file system, place /var on a separate partition
Disable drivers like USB storage when not used, to prevent unauthorized storage or data theft
Check DNS configuration for the dns domain name
Purge old/removed packages (190 found) with aptitude purge or dpkg --purge command. This will cleanup old configuration files, cron jobs and startup scripts.
Install debsums utility for the verification of packages with known good database.
Install package apt-show-versions for patch management purposes
Install a package audit tool to determine vulnerable packages
Remove any unneeded kernel packages
Determine if protocol 'dccp' is really needed on this system
Determine if protocol 'sctp' is really needed on this system
Determine if protocol 'rds' is really needed on this system
Determine if protocol 'tipc' is really needed on this system
Access to CUPS configuration could be more strict.
Enable logging to an external logging host for archiving purposes and additional protection
Check what deleted files are still in use and why.
Add a legal banner to /etc/issue, to warn unauthorized users
Add legal banner to /etc/issue.net, to warn unauthorized users
Enable process accounting
Enable sysstat to collect accounting (disabled)
Determine the location of auditd configuration file
Check output of aa-status
Install a file integrity tool to monitor changes to critical and sensitive files
Consider restricting file permissions
Double check the permissions of home directories as some might be not strict enough.
One or more sysctl values differ from the scan profile and could be tweaked
Harden compilers like restricting access to root user only
Harden the system by installing at least one malware scanner, to perform periodic file system scans
